History of Present Illness (HPI) Eleanor Martinez is a 61‑year‑old woman with a recent diagnosis of stage IIIB (T4N2M0) squamous cell carcinoma of the left upper lobe, initially presented with persistent cough, dyspnea on exertion, and a 6‑kg weight loss over two months. She underwent bronchoscopic core biopsy confirming squamous histology (p40‑positive, TTF‑1‑negative) and next‑generation sequencing that revealed a TP53 missense mutation (p.R273C) and CDKN2A homozygous deletion; no actionable driver alterations (EGFR, ALK, ROS1, BRAF) were identified. One month after initial diagnosis, a contrast‑enhanced chest CT demonstrated a 5.2 cm spiculated left upper lobe mass with ipsilateral mediastinal lymphadenopathy. She received palliative external‑beam radiation to the primary lesion (30 Gy/10 fractions) for symptom control. At age 61, a contrast‑enhanced brain MRI identified three enhancing lesions (0.8 cm right frontal, 0.6 cm left frontal, 0.5 cm left cerebellar) consistent with metastatic disease. She reports mild headache but no focal neurological deficits. ECOG performance status remains 2 (ambulatory, capable of self‑care but unable to carry out work activities). The current discussion focuses on optimal local therapy for the brain metastases and integration with systemic treatment planning. ### 3.
